overall: The AG found the committee violated the Open Meeting Law by late approval of executive session minutes, failing to periodically review them for release, insufficiently detailed minutes, and voting on a pay raise in executive session; it rejected the records-request and intent allegations.

allegations.summary: A public records request for executive session minutes was said to require the committee to review those minutes for release under the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the request for meeting minutes was not a request that fell under the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, § 22(c), (g)(2), and did not impose upon the Committee the additional obligation to review its executive session minutes for possible public release.

allegations.summary: The committee allegedly failed to timely approve numerous executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: As these minutes were not approved within three meetings or 30 days, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The committee allegedly failed to periodically review its outstanding executive session minutes to determine whether they could be released.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee went two years or longer between reviews, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to review its executive session minutes at reasonable intervals to determine whether continued nondisclosure was warranted or whether the minutes could be released to the public.

allegations.summary: Many executive session minutes were allegedly insufficiently detailed, some only citing the executive session purpose instead of summarizing discussion.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to draft and approve accurate minutes for dozens of executive sessions from 2014 through 2018.

allegations.summary: The committee allegedly voted in executive session to give the superintendent a retroactive 3% pay increase for 2014-2015.
allegations.key_passage: Although negotiation of the Superintendent’s contract was an appropriate subject for executive session, once the negotiations concluded, the Committee was obligated to return to open session to vote to execute the contract extension.

allegations.summary: The complainant urged that the violations were intentional; the AG considered whether an intentional violation under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c) was shown.
allegations.key_passage: Here, notwithstanding a lengthy pattern of committing the same types of Open Meeting Law violations, particularly with regard to meeting minutes, we find no specific evidence that the Committee intentionally violated the Law or acted with deliberate ignorance of the Law’s requirements.

allegations.summary: The complaint alleged minutes gave no specific justification for using the litigation purpose (Purpose 3) in several executive sessions.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
All committee members must attend an Open Meeting Law training webinar provided by the AG's office within ninety days of receipt of the letter.
Create sufficiently detailed minutes for the 1/8/2018, 1/29/2018, 2/12/2018, 4/2/2018, 4/30/2018, 5/14/2018, and 6/4/2018 executive sessions to the best of its ability.
Certify compliance with the order to the AG's office within ninety days of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
